Latest Update: 'Bitter' Romelu Lukaku set to 'drop a bombshell' on Belgian football following his shock retirement, claims former team-mate after one-hour phone call

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (978 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 04:37 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 04:38 EST, 24 November 2026.
  • Radja Nainggolan has claimed his former team-mate Romelu Lukaku is planning a 'bombshell' statement on Belgian football following his shock retirement from the national team.
  • Lukaku, 33, unexpectedly announced his retirement from international football following Belgium's Nations League matches against Turkey and Italy earlier this month.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MICHAEL PAVITT, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 04:37 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 04:38 EST, 24 November 2026.

Radja Nainggolan has claimed his former team-mate Romelu Lukaku is planning a 'bombshell' statement on Belgian football following his shock retirement from the national team.

Lukaku, 33, unexpectedly announced his retirement from international football following Belgium's Nations League matches against Turkey and Italy earlier this month.

Belgium's all-time record goalscorer had been left on the bench against Italy, while he had not been in the squad three days earlier for the match against Turkey.

Lukaku's shock announcement caught Belgian media by surprise, while his former international team-mate Nainggolan has claimed more news will follow from the star.

Nainggolan, who won 30 caps for the national team between 2009 and 2018, revealed on the Ongefilterd Voetbal podcast he had a one-hour phone call with Lukaku following his decision.

The former Inter Milan and Roma midfielder stated that Lukaku told him: 'You are only allowed to say that a bombshell is about to explode.'.

Romelu Lukaku confirmed his shock retirement from international football earlier this month.

According to recent reports, former team-mate Radja Nainggolan claims Lukaku is planning a 'bombshell' statement for Belgian football following a one hour phone call with the star. Source: Ongefilterd Voetbal.

'So something is still coming,' Nainggolan noted.

According to recent reports, 'What? I don't know. There were some internal problems between him and a certain person. But I'm not going to say much about that.

Sources indicate that 'Romelu will bring that up himself. He was a bit bitter, though. He was disappointed, frustrated.

'We will hear from him soon what will happen.

'About the real problems that were at play, he will be able to explain that better than I.'.

Lukaku's retirement had marked a stunning reversal of his looks, with the former Chelsea and Manchester United forward having vowed in January that the 2026 World Cup would not be his last major tournament with the Belgium national team.

Describing his international career as a 'great ride', Lukaku had confirmed his international retirement on social media.

Industry observers note that '16 years old', his Instagram statement began. 'For 16 years, I gave everything for the national team. I experienced every possible emotion. I played with fantastic teammates for whom I will always be grateful.

Lukaku vowed in January that the 2026 World Cup would not be his last major tournament.

The Belgian forward has fallen down the pecking order and spent a lot of time on the bench.

'I want to thank them all. I also want to thank all the coaches for pushing me and giving me the confidence to help the team. It was a great ride, and I enjoyed every moment.

It has been revealed that 'To the Belgian fans, thank you for the support you have given our team. I am proud to have represented my country at four World Cups and three European Championships. I will never forget those moments. I am at peace with my decision to stop here. It was amazing, it was a joy. I am grateful. Thank you.'.

The Belgian veteran accompanied his post with a gallery of photographs from his storied international career, from his debut against Croatia under Dick Advocaat in 2010 to his final chapter wearing the armband.

Lukaku has captained Belgium on a handful of occasions since 2020, alongside the likes of Kevin De Bruyne and Youri Tielemans.

The 33-year-old forward, who became one of the hottest properties in world football after breaking onto the scene at Chelsea, has been a regular fixture in the international set-up for almost two decades.

Spearheading Belgium's golden generation, which included star-studded talents such as De Bruyne, Thibaut Courtois and Eden Hazard, Lukaku chalked up an impressive 135 caps for the international team.

He also retired as Belgium's all-time top scorer on 94 goals, just six shy of a century.

After suffering multiple injury setbacks, he featured at the 2026 World Cup under Rudi Garcia and continued to play a crucial role, scoring three times as a substitute to guide Belgium to the quarter-finals where they were ultimately stopped by eventual champions Spain.

Since Mark van Bommel's appointment in August, following Garcia's departure at the end of his contract, Lukaku has slipped further down the pecking order, with Charles De Ketelaere preferred to lead the line.

During Belgium's resounding 4-1 victory over Italy on Sunday, Lukaku warmed the bench as an unused substitute – and wasn't even in the squad to face Turkey three days before.

Lukaku, pictured with Kevin De Bruyne, was an unused substitute as Belgium beat Italy 4-1.

While Belgium were winning in the second half against the Italians, Lukaku was seen warming up on the sidelines in the hope of featuring for one last time, but unfortunately was not given the opportunity.

VTM NIEUWS anchor Maarten Breckx claimed De Bruyne looked 'concerned' while speaking to Lukaku on the bench, suggesting the former Man City star was unhappy to see his team-mate overlooked.

Industry observers note that 'When it became clear that he wouldn't be allowed to come on, De Bruyne was talking to him. You could see the concern in his eyes,' he stated.

Recent findings suggest that 'You could tell, especially from Romelu's attitude, that he was dissatisfied and displeased. He had probably counted on getting some minutes...'.

With only Jan Vertonghen and Axel Witsel registering more international caps than Lukaku over their careers, boasting 157 and 140 appearances respectively, Belgium are expected to give the 33-year-old forward a send-off he deserves in the near future.

Witsel, who also called time on his Belgium career this year, was one of the team-mates to celebrate Lukaku's retirement on Instagram.

It has been revealed that 'Thanks for everything, legend. Thank you, what a journey we've had together,' he wrote.

73 goals from dropping deep - we ask Kane to break down how he did it

📅 04 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1775 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Harry Kane is one of the leading names in the race for this year's Ballon d'Or, having scored 73 goals last season for club and country.
  • As Harry Kane's career has progressed, the 33-year-old has taken an increasingly complete role, popping up to collect the ball as deep as his own box.
  • Many wonder why a talisman tasked with scoring doesn't spend more time closer to goal, but last season the England and Bayern Munich striker scored 73 goals - the highest tally of his career - while playing deeper than he ever has done.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Harry Kane is one of the leading names in the race for this year's Ballon d'Or, having scored 73 goals last season for club and country.

As Harry Kane's career has progressed, the 33-year-old has taken an increasingly complete role, popping up to collect the ball as deep as his own box.

Many wonder why a talisman tasked with scoring doesn't spend more time closer to goal, but last season the England and Bayern Munich striker scored 73 goals - the highest tally of his career - while playing deeper than he ever has done.

When I mention this paradox, a grin spreads across his face.

"Until you really understand football and understand what we've been talking about, it's so easy to say 'stay high, you're going to score' but it doesn't work like that," Kane says.

I sat down to speak to Kane about the finer details of his game, shedding light on his unique role.

Industry observers note that watching Kane train, his professionalism is palpable. England's record goalscorer is one of the first out on the pitch. The younger players indulge in playful kick-ups as he watches, engaged in conversation with a member of staff.

From a distance, that makes it easy to confuse him with a coach but, given his role on the pitch, it is a fitting mistake.

Kane's style of play reflects who he is as a person, with those who know him saying he is well-rounded and humble on and off the pitch.

How dropping deep helps Kane score.

The season is in its infancy but Kane isn't basking in the success of the past 12 months. With only five days of pre-season training under his belt, the England captain completed 90 minutes of Bayern's 2-1 win over Borussia Dortmund to lift the German Super Cup.

As demanding as his roaming role is, he has taken the physical demands of it in his stride. Across the past six seasons, STATSports - a sports technology company Kane has invested in - found his distance covered, high-speed running and accelerations were up 8%, 22% and 42% respectively.

And given how the tactical landscape has changed over that time, it is particularly impressive Kane has been able to not only keep up, but stay ahead.

Kane's role has evolved drastically over the past nine years, with the striker now heavily involved in all phases of the game -Â including as deep as his own box.

"Over the last five or six years, man-to-man pressure has become bigger," Kane states.

"European football is physical and top teams are trying to win the ball back high, trusting their defenders and midfielders to defend man for man to win their battles.".

Given that change, the best teams have recruited physical athletes and brilliant dribblers who can beat their man when the game becomes a series of one-against-ones.

Kane, not known for his dribbling - and by his own admission "not the fastest", has thrived on his own terms.

In a recent development, against Dortmund, there was a specific moment Kane dropped deep, looking to arrive in space unmarked. Recognising the danger, two players converged on the Englishman.

It has been revealed that kane's dribbling is cerebral. His speed of thought provides him solutions to problems others would attempt to solve with their feet alone.

According to recent reports, after getting low and using his strength to shrug centre-back Waldemar Anton off him, Kane rose, slightly adjusting his body to the right. These micro-adjustments are a hallmark of his game and through them he is able to shift an entire team's momentum.

Fooled by this feint, Daniel Svensson and Jobe Bellingham found themselves wrong-footed as Kane snapped the ball back the other way, opening up the entire pitch from within Bayern's half.

Kane wins his individual battle with Waldemar Anton, shielding the ball and showcasing strength.

As he rises, he positions his body to the right, facing his own goal.

Through clever body positioning, Kane moves the opposition towards the right side of the pitch. This is his cue to cut the ball back into the open space.

This allows Kane to evade two defenders, now facing the opposition's goal.

Earlier this year, Bayern boss Vincent Kompany shed light on Kane's unique role, explaining it as being 50% coached and 50% Kane deciding what to do.

In a recent development, "I think it's partly instinct, using my football brain and getting the feeling on the pitch," indicates Kane. "If, for example, I want to drop and see if the centre-back really wants to commit, he might commit into midfield, but is he going to commit if I drop all the way to my box?

"After the first five or 10 minutes you really get an understanding of how the opposition are going to play, which dictates how I play.".

In a recent development, in the second minute of Bayern Munich's game against Arsenal, Kane dropped deep into a position normally occupied by centre-backs. Arsenal centre-back William Saliba marked him all the way, vacating space higher up the pitch.

There is a shared understanding at Bayern of an approach that allows team-mates to make sense of rotations that, to the naked eye, appear random.

Kane, who is given more freedom than most, is at the centre of it.

Recent findings suggest that "I feel like my position now is as one of two 10s, and you work together," he says. "You can double up on one side to overload, which causes the opposition centre-backs a problem of who to mark.

"If they want to mark both, they've got to go man-to-man and then that leaves space for our wingers or full-backs to run into.

"It's posing all these questions to the opposition but, personally, I love having someone close to me who I can link with.".

Kane built his reputation playing as a lone number nine, so it is interesting to hear him identify instead as a number 10 -Â in a front two.

"When you're the number nine on your own you can get marked by two centre-backs and you struggle to get touches on the ball," he claims. "You're relying on everyone else to find you with the ball.".

Showing Kane two clips from last season, I ask him to talk through what was going through his head.

"The thing with our formation is, as long as there's someone in each position, it doesn't really matter who it is. Lucho [Luis Diaz] in this clip is playing as one of those 10s.

"I've come off to try and create a bit of space and Lucho's gone through the centre.".

Distracted by Kane's dropping-deep movement, one of the opposition midfielders is pulled towards him. This creates space, allowing Joshua Kimmich to punch the ball through to Diaz.

It has been revealed that "I think it's Serge [Gnabry] making the run in behind which takes the defenders back, which allows me and Lucho that space in between. Lucho lays it off and whenever I'm in that position, around 20-25 yards out, I'm always looking if I can get my shot off.".

It is one of many examples of Kane initially dropping deep before scoring.

"By playing deep when the play develops, I end up coming into a number 10 spot when everyone's dropped," he states. "I can get shots off from the edge of the box, which is a massive strength of mine, or I'm running off the back of players where no-one's picking me up - because the midfielder finds it hard to [track].".

The Frankfurt midfielder notices Kane dropping deep. Recognising this danger, he moves towards him.

According to recent reports, with Frankfurt's central midfielder pulled towards Kane, Luis Diaz is able to receive a pass between the lines. He forms a central front two with Kane. The wingers ahead of them, Serge Gnabry and Michael Olise, push the defensive line back.

Kane is found in space around the edge of the box and strikes the ball hard into the net.

The second clip is from Bayern's Champions League tie against Club Brugge.

Usually Kane is marked by an opposition centre-back, but the Belgian club give that responsibility to their holding midfielder -Â something he recognises and exploits.

Lennart Karl scores without Kane touching the ball, but the striker's involvement is undeniable.

"These are the little runs, again, not everyone sees," Kane explains. "With Jamal Musiala and Lenny, they're so good at receiving the ball and dribbling so there'll be times where I will actually stay higher and let those guys get on the ball a bit deeper, and I'll try and make runs in behind.

"Without changing my game too much, I try and complement the players around me.

"I know Lenny is so good in those pockets and when he gets there, I'm more thinking of running in behind because, one, he can play me in and I can go through on goal, or two, he can dribble with the ball and do exactly what happened here.

"As soon as Lenny gets in that pocket I make the run and not always to get the ball, sometimes it is just to drag the defender away.

"Now he's one-against-one with a centre-back in the middle of the pitch and that's dangerous for any centre-back.".

In a recent development, karl receives the ball in the middle of the pitch. As seen in yellow, Kane is being marked by Club Brugge's holding midfielder, rather than any of the central defenders.

Kane, recognising this, makes a diagonal run in behind, pulling the opposition holding midfielder away from the centre of the pitch.

Karl drives with the ball into the space created by Kane before putting the ball into the top corner.

It has been revealed that with the Ballon d'Or announcement on the horizon, Kane's name is in the conversation, primarily for the sheer volume of goals he has scored. What is easier to miss in that debate is the rest of his game.

Kane plays for the team in each phase of the game across the entirety of the pitch, while at the same time producing extraordinary individual numbers that match the likes of Cristiano Ronaldo, Lionel Messi and Erling Haaland.

He has described himself as playing in the role of a number 10, nine and six at times.

In a football world of specific and heavily drilled tactical roles, that is quite the achievement.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that there is no more room for error in the 2026-27 UEFA Women's Champions League. After four matchdays, the league phase has been whittled down to only two games left for each of the 18 clubs, and the margin between a bye into the quarterfinals and an extra round of knockout playoffs in February will come down to dwindling points.

In a recent development, OL Lyonnes rule the league phase at the moment. They top the tournament table with ten points, level with FC Barcelona but with a superior goal difference. Just behind the two Champions League contenders are Bayern Munich and Arsenal, with Chelsea FC and Manchester City creeping closer to the top four. Out of the 18 clubs competing, only four will earn direct berths to the quarterfinals, and eight will compete for a future spot alongside them.

The final six clubs with the least amount of points will see their Champions League dream end, so matchday 5 will be a crucial turning point for several teams.

Sources indicate that fighting for top spot positioning will be Arsenal and OL Lyonnes, and Chelsea against Paris Saint-Germain. HB Koge, Roma, and tournament debutants Inter Milan are level on four points and need to be in full urgency mode if they're to leapfrog and remain in contention for future rounds.

Here's what to watch on Matchday 5:.

Wednesday, Nov. 18BK Hacken vs. Manchester City, 12:45 p.m. (Paramount+)Real Madrid vs. Inter, 12:45 p.m. (Paramount+)   Chelsea vs. Paris Saint-Germain, 3 p.m. (Paramount+)   Juventus vs. OH Leuven, 3 p.m. (Paramount+)  Thursday, Nov. 19 Austria Wien vs. Bayern Munich, 12:45 p.m. (Paramount+)   Paris FC vs. HB Koge, 12:45 p.m. (Paramount+)  Arsenal vs. OL Lyonnes, 3 p.m. (Paramount+)   Barcelona vs. Servette, 3 p.m. (Paramount+)  Benfica vs. Roma, 3 p.m. (Paramount+).

Fans could get a glimpse of a future round when Arsenal take on OL Lyonnes on Thursday. The Gunners now have the tall task of tackling the French giants after battling Barcelona to a 1-1 draw at Camp Nou last week.

A strong team defensive performance, anchored by goalkeeper Misa Rodriguez against the current title holders, and the inclusion of Frida Maanum in the attack were key difference-makers. Manager Renee Slegers and her side seem to be turning the page, with better results after questionable tactics and player availability raised concerns about the club's earlier performances.

Taking on OL Lyonnes also won't be easy. The top French side has scored 20 goals through four league phase matches, and Marie-Antoinette Katoto leads the competition's Golden Boot race with seven goals. U.S. women's national team defensive midfielder Lily Yohannes is getting more lethal in the tournament and scored in her second consecutive tournament match during OL's 6-0 blowout against Juventus.

Lily Yohannes makes it FOUR 💥The USWNT midfielder has now scored in back-to-back UWCL matches 🇺🇸🔥Stream every UEFA Women’s Champions League game on @paramountplus 📺 pic.twitter.com/9uLM309RM4.

The eight-time Champions League winners will go up against an English club with plenty of momentum following last week's results against Barcelona. The Gunners have more players available to shake things up on the pitch, and Alessia Russo remains a threat after her hat trick against Benfica and has four goals in the league phase.

Chelsea FC will host PSG and the Blues are riding high on stout defensive performances. They co-lead the tournament alongside OL Lyonnes with zero goals conceded through four league phase games.

The London side will need to be far better in attack if they want to claim being a top contender, though it's not for lack of trying. They're coming off a scoreless draw against BK Hacken, where they recorded a whopping 32 shots but only six attempts on target. U.S. women's national team winger Alyssa Thompson is still a factor with her swift technique and could help stretch PSG's backline, while Wieke Kaptein gets into dangerous spaces. Kaptein created both goals in Chelsea's 2-0 win against Roma, and the Dutch player has one goal and two assists in the tournament.

PSG's fortunes seem to be turning for the worse after a promising start to the competition. They're in 10th place on the table now with five points and just one win in their last four games. The loss of Sakina Karchaoui with an ankle injury for the remainder of the league phase is a blow to the roster, though Naomie Feller, with two goals and two assists, is a threat for the Parisians.

Industry observers note that there are plenty of teams on the lower side of the table and running out of time. Alongside PSG with necessary urgency are Juventus, who were just beaten by OL Lyonnes, 6-0, and face a desperate 17th-place OH Leuven before closing out the league phase against PSG. It makes the penultimate meeting with OH Leuven almost a must win for Juventus, to lessen the stress on the final matchday.

A particularly intriguing matchup between ninth-place Benfica and 12th-place Roma could shake up the league table with a win by either side. If Roma's Kayleigh van Dooren and Alayah Pilgrim stay active on offense again, it could be a tough challenge for Benfica.

Hashim Thaci's second conviction in The Hague reignites debate in Kosovo about justice and the Kosovo Specialist Chambers

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (896 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A court in The Hague on Tuesday convicted former Kosovo President Hashim Thaci of obstructing justice and attempting to influence witnesses during his recent war crimes trial and sentenced him to 17 months in prison.
  • This term will be added to his 25-year sentence for war crimes, which was handed down by the same court, the Kosovo Specialist Chambers, on September 16.
  • According to the indictment of the Specialist Prosecutor's Office, Thaci had provided visitors at the detention facility in The Hague with confidential information about witnesses in his war crimes trial and had instructed them on how to influence their testimony.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A court in The Hague on Tuesday convicted former Kosovo President Hashim Thaci of obstructing justice and attempting to influence witnesses during his recent war crimes trial and sentenced him to 17 months in prison.

This term will be added to his 25-year sentence for war crimes, which was handed down by the same court, the Kosovo Specialist Chambers, on September 16.

According to the indictment of the Specialist Prosecutor's Office, Thaci had provided visitors at the detention facility in The Hague with confidential information about witnesses in his war crimes trial and had instructed them on how to influence their testimony.

Three other men — former head of the Kosovo Intelligence Agency Bashkim Smakaj, former Minister of Justice Hajredin Kuci, and Fadil Fazliu — were also convicted.

Sources indicate that thaci, who was the former political leader of the Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA) during the 1998-1999 Kosovo War, is viewed by many in his home country as a hero. His war crimes conviction in September was greeted in Kosovo with anger and dismay.

Thaci has vowed to appeal the war crimes conviction.

His two convictions touch deep sensitivities in Kosovo society. Tuesday's ruling brings renewed attention to the war that ended 27 years ago, the role played by its former leaders, and the continuing debate over justice, individual or collective responsibility for the KLA's war to liberate Kosovo from Serbia, and trust in judicial institutions.

The response from the government of Kosovo was swift.

It has been revealed that in a statement issued on Tuesday, the government said, "Trust in justice is built not only on the decisions that are made, but also on the manner in which they are reached. Therefore, our commitment to the rule of law and our insistence on the full respect of rights and procedural guarantees are part of the same principled position: Justice must not only be done, but must also be fair, transparent, and credible.".

The Kosovo Specialist Chambers was established in 2015 by the parliament of Kosovo at the instigation of the European Union and the United States.

The court was created to investigate serious crimes allegedly committed by members of the KLA during and after the Kosovo War.

For security reasons, including concerns about witness intimidation, the court was located in The Hague in the Netherlands.

After Thaci and three others were convicted of war crimes in first instance in September, Kosovo's state authorities established a working group to draft a strategy regarding the appeal proceedings before the Kosovo Specialist Chambers.

The group is chaired by Foreign Minister Glauk Konjufca and includes members of Kosovo's parliament.

Prime Minister Albin Kurti has stated that the working group continues to believe that "the first-instance judgment of the Specialist Chambers is unjust, both legally and morally," and that as a result, "the government is working to secure a correction at the appeals level before the Specialist Chambers.".

In addition, the parliament of Kosovo is currently considering amendments to the law governing the Kosovo Specialist Chambers.

The draft law, which is expected to be adopted, envisages narrowing the court's mandate in several areas, including the time period covered by its jurisdiction, limiting the maximum prison sentence to 15 years, allowing sentences to be served in Kosovo, and introducing the possibility of presidential pardons for persons convicted by final court decisions.

How do political analysts and legal experts view the parliament's attempt to amend the law on the Kosovo Specialist Chambers before the judicial process involving the four men convicted of war crimes has reached a final verdict?

"From an international perspective, at first glance, this initiative could even be interpreted as an attempt to interfere in the judicial process," said political analyst and university professor Artan Muhaxheri.

"Precisely for this reason, it is essential that Kosovo's political spectrum and its legal experts demonstrate beyond any doubt that this measure does not conflict with Kosovo's international obligations toward the European Union," Muhaxheri told DW, adding that this is the only way to ensure that the desired outcome is achieved and that the initiative does not produce the opposite effect.

"Issues relating to jurisdiction, statutory limits on maximum sentences, and other similar matters must be argued professionally and rigorously, demonstrating that they fully guarantee judicial independence and enjoy solid support within Kosovo's legal system, the same legal system that, first and foremost, established the Specialist Chambers," he stated.

Ehat Miftaraj, executive director of the Kosovo Law Institute (IKD), told DW that although the Kosovo Specialist Chambers were established by the Republic of Kosovo itself, "the way the judicial process has unfolded has created the impression that judges, prosecutors and certain international actors have treated not only the accused but also Kosovo itself with distrust, prejudice, and an often condescending approach.".

Miftaraj went on to say that reactions and objections in Kosovo to the decisions of the Specialist Chambers are also interpreted and judged in the historical and emotional context of the war and what Kosovo's citizens experienced during and after it.

In a recent development, "In a democratic society, every citizen, including political and institutional representatives, has the right to criticize judicial decisions," he remarked. "However, there is a fundamental distinction between criticism based on legal arguments and attempts to delegitimize courts or exert influence over judicial proceedings. And here, there is room for criticism of both sides.".

Industry observers note that in a farewell for Mauricio Pochettino before he heads to Manchester United, the United States men's national team were able to defeat Haiti 2-0 on Tuesday night, advancing in the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals 8-0 on aggregate. Christian Pulisic opened the scoring with a bicycle-kick goal to kick things off, which was the emphatic send-off that was needed prior to Pochettino arriving in Manchester, but the USMNT were able to keep things up in the celebration in Cincinnati.

CHRISTIAN PULISIC GET ON YOUR BIKE‼️#USMNT x @VW pic.twitter.com/Yb3yqXfC33.

Julian Hall followed with a poacher's goal as Weston McKennie played orchestrator, and it continued a theme that whoever ends up taking over the national team will have tough decisions ahead. Folarin Balogun is struggling for minutes with Monaco and is looking to make a move at the end of the season, and Hall has done everything that he can to increase his own standing with five goals in six games for the USMNT.

In a recent development, the New York Red Bulls star has a ways to go considering that he's still only 18 and will need to gain experience against top teams in the world instead of just Haiti, but he also can't ask for a better start than what he has gotten off to. It's why this is such an attractive job for whoever takes over the USMNT. They'll be able to build upon the good that Pochettino has instilled; the talent is there to move the squad forward, and there's plenty to love about the youth of the USMNT.

Recent findings suggest that and alongside that, Pulisic has essentially screamed don't forget about me. During this camp, the Milan man has followed up on signing a new contract with the club by reaching 35 national team goals, moving into fourth all time for the USMNT over Eric Wynalda. Diego Kochen added to the good vibes with a third straight clean sheet, and Neil Pierre was even able to be cap-tied against the nation that he's also eligible for as the full-circle moments were left and right.

Pulisic, the former 17-year-old phenom, was subbed off for Cavan Sullivan, the current 17-year-old phenom, and while the goal difference may have been larger in the first leg between these sides, this felt like a more measured performance despite the strangeness of Pochettino's assistants heading to United while he managed the squad prior to catching his own charter.

It has been revealed that this camp had every chance of being a disaster given the circumstances of Pochettino leaving, but all parties did what was needed during this camp. All dual nationals were capped, including Santiago Castaneda, showing that even on his way out, Pochettino made sure to take care of the future of the federation. On to the next round of the Concacaf Nations League with a newly introduced manager and no complaints with the performance so far for the squad.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 05:07 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 05:13 EST, 24 November 2026.
  • Premier League clubs are bracing themselves for a new raid of their talent from Saudi Arabia, as the mega-money league considers relaxing spending rules.
  • Teams in the Saudi Pro League (SPL) are currently only allowed eight foreign players in their 25-man squads but are discussing increasing that number to 14 or even higher.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 05:07 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 05:13 EST, 24 November 2026.

Premier League clubs are bracing themselves for a new raid of their talent from Saudi Arabia, as the mega-money league considers relaxing spending rules.

Teams in the Saudi Pro League (SPL) are currently only allowed eight foreign players in their 25-man squads but are discussing increasing that number to 14 or even higher.

If the move is approved, it is likely to trigger a flood of cash in the market similar to the massive £765million spree in 2023 that saw the likes of Cristiano Ronaldo, Karim Benzema and N'Golo Kante sign for Public Investment Fund (PIF) teams.

In that 2023 window, almost half of the transfer fees received by Premier League clubs came from the SPL.

In total, 94 players were signed by Pro League clubs and the January transfer window could now follow a similar pattern.

The Saudi spending reached such astronomic levels that it eclipsed every other league in Europe aside from the Premier League.

Cristiano Ronaldo (right) and Angelo, pictured in action for Al Nassr, are among the foreign stars already plying their trade in Saudi Arabia and more will be on their way.

The supposed reason for the proposed rule change is to elevate the standard of existing Saudi players at home by raising the overall level of talent ahead of the country hosting the World Cup in 2034.

But critics argue that the newly introduced rules would only force Saudi players out of their domestic league in place of high-profile foreign recruits.

While Premier League clubs are often reluctant to allow talent to leave in January midway through the season, the fees on offer from Saudi can be eye-watering and hard to turn down.

Aston Villa sold Jhon Duran and later Ollie Watkins for a combined £115million to the SPL.

Fulham accepted £50m for Aleksandar Mitrovic, while Wolves banked £47m for Ruben Neves and Liverpool were able to recoup almost £50m for Darwin Nunez.

West Ham were able to cash in on Crysencio Summerville after relegation last term when Al Hilal bought him for £60m.

Would Man United consider offers for Bruno Fernandes as his contract winds down? Or will they keep the club captain to help battle relegation?

Suddenly every Premier League club recruitment department will be reassessing their squads and be keeping a close eye on the rule developments in Saudi.

Ollie Watkins moved from Aston Villa to Al Hilal and the Premier League side have recouped huge fees from the SPL in the  past.

Ivan Toney (second from left) and his Al Ahli team-mates celebrate a goal against Al Nassr.

The SPL's decision on whether to allow the increase of foreign players will be clarified before the winter window opens.

The PIF are winding down their investment in golf through LIV having invested more than £3.7billion since 2021 but their operation in football indicates no sign of slowing down.

Players weighing up a move to Saudi will perhaps have a more difficult decision than in 2023 over relocating, with conflict still affecting the country.

The Asian Cup was postponed earlier in November following a missile attack from Yemen-based Houthi rebels on Riyadh airport that killed 13 people and injured more than 300.

Security fears and geo-political uncertainty could make footballers think twice before accepting the lucrative contracts on offer in January and beyond.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, for the first time in 616 days, Tottenham Hotspur have won three Premier League matches in a row.
  • This victory over Crystal Palace was not as impressive as last week’s triumph at Chelsea, but it did not need to be.
  • Roberto De Zerbi’s team ended the night with 34 shots to Palace’s two and with 758 completed passes to Palace’s 149.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, for the first time in 616 days, Tottenham Hotspur have won three Premier League matches in a row. Three different managers have been sacked in that time, and the mood in north London had plunged to grim lows, but finally there is a sense that something truly exciting is stirring at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

This victory over Crystal Palace was not as impressive as last week’s triumph at Chelsea, but it did not need to be. After Palace striker Jean-Philippe Mateta was sent off in the 13th minute, Spurs simply had to make their numerical advantage count. They did so with relative ease, taking complete control of possession and creating endless goalscoring opportunities.

Roberto De Zerbi’s team ended the night with 34 shots to Palace’s two and with 758 completed passes to Palace’s 149. The goals ultimately came from two defenders, Archie Gray and Jan Paul van Hecke, but there was a long list of Spurs players who might have scored here.

According to recent reports, spurs take the lead through an Archie Gray header! ⚪ https://t.co/qSCECkOJur.

In a recent development, did this defeat mark the end for Pierre Sage, the Palace manager? The Frenchman was only appointed in June but it has been a grisly start to the campaign. Palace have the worst defence in the league, have lost six of nine games and have not produced any truly encouraging performances in the Premier League.

Even in the two games Palace have won, against Fulham and Nottingham Forest, they were lucky to do so. The likes of Sean Dyche and Thomas Frank, both of whom would be strong candidates to replace Sage if Palace do pull the trigger, will no doubt have been keeping an eye on events here.

In a recent development, “I am really aware of the situation,” Sage stated. “I don’t like this situation. [But] you can trust in me, I will never give up. I want to be the first on the pitch on Monday. I have the rage to train more. It’s not me to decide this thing [his future]. If I have one hour, I will give my best for one hour. If I have 10 years, I will give my best for 10 years.”.

The decision for Palace chairman Steve Parish, then, is whether this result represented a continuation of the team’s problems or was an aberration caused by the early red card. It would be reasonable for Sage to claim this match was out of his hands from the moment Mateta lunged at Spurs captain Micky van de Ven, but such an argument might not carry much weight with Palace sitting 18th in the table.

In a recent development, the challenge was foolish in the extreme by Mateta, a player who was much more successful in exiting this game than he has been in his numerous attempts to leave Palace in recent transfer windows. At first glance it did not seem the worst tackle, but the replays were damning: Mateta led with his studs and made forceful contact with Van de Ven’s ankle.

It was an inexcusably brainless act, after just 13 minutes of play, and the same could be remarked of Palace’s defending from a right-wing corner a few minutes later. Mohammed Kudus swirled the delivery to the back post, where Gray was unmarked. Yes, Palace were defending with 10. But no, that does not justify the inability of Sage’s players to spot Gray. Even more embarrassingly, the Tottenham player was unmarked again from another corner shortly afterwards.

Industry observers note that it was not the first time this season that Palace’s cause has been undermined by a red card. When they lost at home to Ipswich Town in September, Axel Disasi was sent off after 34 minutes. An absence of discipline? Perhaps. Sage might argue, though, that he is not responsible for his players demonstrating a lack of basic brainpower.

According to recent reports, “Now we are playing as a team,” De Zerbi remarked. “Before the international break, we were playing as many good players but not as a team. We indicated our maturity. We are improving.”.

The second goal was always coming and it arrived in the 73rd minute, when Van Hecke attacked a wonderful cross by Mateus Fernandes. Palace goalkeeper Dean Henderson saved the first attempt but the ball dropped onto the head of Van Hecke, now seated in the six-yard box, and he happily nodded it home.

Roberto De Zerbi, the Spurs head coach, had some good news for the supporters on Friday when he said that James Maddison was fit and available despite being taken off at Stamford Bridge. “This week he didn’t work like the other players, but for tomorrow he is available and he is a special player for us. A special player because of the character and he has unique characteristics.

“For James Maddison or the players who are coming from a long injury, they have to work more than the other players, but he has already four or five weeks he is working very hard and consistently.”.

In a recent development, while Tottenham are chasing a third successive league victory for the first time in 616 day, De Zerbi insisted there will be no complacency. “For me nothing has changed. We started this pre-season with a long project and we have to stay calm and clear in the head to work to build something better than when we came here,” he mentioned. “One win or one defeat more, nothing will change. We have to analyse to improve the results but to improve the results we have to improve all aspects.”.

Pierre Sage, the Palace manager, lightened the load after knocking Fulham out of the Carabao Cup in midweek but seemed surprised that the fans have remained so supportive. “It’s always a good sign,” he noted. “I appreciate it [singing his name at Craven Cottage] very much and I can thank them but I prefer they are with the team than me alone. Because I’m the manager, but I’m not the most vital part of the team, of the performance and the result. I think the players need it more than me but it’s really appreciated from me.”.

Asked what he has learnt about fan sentiment from looking at social media, he said: “I think they understood what happened, why we are not perfect at the moment. We don’t care who is the most responsible for the situation. I take the responsibility. I have no problem with that. I just want people to understand what we do and why.”.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League encounter between Tottenham and Crystal Palace.

Last weekend, Spurs enjoyed a historic result, beating Chelsea 2-0 at Stamford Bridge for only the second time in the league for 36 years thanks to Mike Penders’ own goal and Mathys Tel’s stunning solo strike. This result, coupled with the 3-1 victory over Coventry City in their previous home outing, means that Tottenham have won back-to-back league games and are beginning to gather some momentum under Roberto De Zerbi.

In his pre-match press conference, when asked if he’s felt a change in atmosphere after the triumph at Stamford Bridge, De Zerbi replied: “We have not achieved our goal. We want our fans to be happy, not now, at the end of the season. Now we have to push, we have to stay focused, we have to increase the spirit, the appetite to win games in a row. To do that, we have to show if we are good enough. If we are good enough on the pitch, for sure we are ready. In the head, in the mentality, we have to show, because the step of this club is to win games in a row and to be angry day by day, game by game, win by win. One time or two times are not enough.”.

Recent findings suggest that palace have endured a tricky and inconsistent start to the season under their summer appointment Pierre Sage, accumulating just seven points from their opening seven league matches while shipping 17 goals. The 1-0 League Cup victory over Fulham in midweek has momentarily eased the pressure on the Frenchman, but given their newfound success in recent campaigns, fan expectations have risen, with recent performances prompting some cause for concern.

Tottenham remain without the suspended Rodrigo Bentancur, while Xavi Simons, Wilson Odobert, Lucas Bergvall, Savio, Tosin Adarabioyo and Mykhaylo Mudryk are out injured. James Maddison was substituted early in the second half at Chelsea with an apparent groin strain, but De Zerbi insists he’s available for this one. Destiny Udogie could also be involved after recovering from a knee glitch.

The visitors are without the injured trio of Ismaila Sarr, Takehiro Tomiyasu and Chadi Riad, but there’s hope that Quinten Timber and Jorgen Strand Larsen are fit to be involved this evening after they both missed the Fulham victory.

Kick-off is at 17:30, with teams coming shortly.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Going into the summer transfer window as Premier League champions, hope sprang eternal for Arsenal.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Going into the summer transfer window as Premier League champions, hope sprang eternal for Arsenal.

An opportunity to capitalise, encouraged by a sense at Emirates Stadium that their competitors were in transition because of managerial instability.

If ever there was a moment to strike in recruitment, this was it.

Industry observers note that the prepares were ambitious: a shortlist with more than 20 players on it. They were targets at Real Madrid and Atletico Madrid, even at Chelsea and Tottenham.

But as the window shut on Tuesday night, you could not escape the sense of unfulfillment - certainly from a section of supporters.

Arsenal's close season was one characterised by some unquestionable successes, but also riddled by difficulties and frustration.

Ahead of their home match against Chelsea on Sunday, BBC Sport details Arsenal's transfer window and whether manager Mikel Arteta, sporting director Andrea Berta and, perhaps most pertinently, owners Kroenke Sports Entertainment can deem their summer operation a success.

Bruno Guimaraes's Â£75m capture from Newcastle United was Arsenal's most eye-catching signing.

Heading into the summer, Arsenal were keeping abreast of Guimaraes' situation at Newcastle, although others were considered a higher priority.

For instance, their interest in Elliot Anderson was widely reported, but it was clear the England international was joining Manchester City.

Guimaraes' former Newcastle team-mate Sandro Tonali and Bournemouth's Alex Scott were also among the midfielders explored before a move for the South American accelerated.

At the ages of 26 and 23 respectively, Tonali and Scott are younger than Guimaraes, who turns 29 in November.

But numerous factors, including availability and price - Tonali joined Spurs for a minimum Â£92m - made their signings difficult.

Aston Villa's Amadou Onana was also among the options considered, but the Belgium international suffered a serious knee injury at the World Cup.

By mid-June Guimaraes, who had universal backing inside the Emirates, emerged as the club's primary focus.

Berta knew the player's camp well and Guimaraes was admired by Arteta, who had made it clear he wanted proven talent to take his starting XI - rather than the wider squad - to greater heights.

Berta used his strong relationship with Guimaraes' representatives to facilitate Arsenal's move, hence why Newcastle maintained they had had no direct contact from the London club until days before his move was completed.

It is not uncommon for Berta to lean on intermediaries to conduct negotiations, although the approach has had varying degrees of success.

For instance, Arsenal actively sought moves for Leicester City teenagers Jeremy Monga and Louis Page over the summer.

But sources insist that the lack of club-to-club discussions meant both players ultimately did not join Arsenal, with Monga eventually signing for Manchester City when he appeared to be on the verge of moving to the Emirates.

That stated, Berta's success in pivoting the club towards a deal for Guimaraes when it became clear other targets were not viable was well received behind the scenes at Arsenal.

The signing of Ezri Konsa was equally complex. Konsa was viewed internally as Arteta's first-choice defensive option.

Arteta wanted players used to the rigours of Premier League football - hence the moves for Guimaraes, Konsa and the failed efforts to land Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa.

Sources indicate that konsa's ability to play at right-back was also viewed as a major benefit. Arsenal considered signing an orthodox right-back, with Ivan Fresneda among the options, but Konsa's versatility was a key factor.

According to recent reports, but Berta appeared reluctant to meet Villa's valuation. A week before the Konsa deal was confirmed, Arsenal made a Â£40m offer, which was duly rejected.

Sources claim the deal was eventually sealed by the ownership at both clubs, and the transfer was agreed at Â£51m, with Â£4m in add-ons.

In the event of not reaching an agreement for Konsa, it is understood Tottenham duo Cristian Romero and Micky van der Ven were identified as targets â but Arsenal's north London rivals would not consider selling to them.

Como centre-back Jacobo Ramon is a player the club will continue to monitor, but clauses attached to his current contract make the deal difficult.

Tarik Muharemovic, who joined Leeds United, was another considered.

In attack, Christos Tzolis' impact since arriving from Club Brugge in a deal worth about Â£35m means the Greece international has been heralded as one of the discoveries of the summer.

It is understood the potential deal for the former Norwich winger was initially raised by an intermediary close to a senior member of the coaching staff during the close season.

Berta's number two, Maurizio Micheli, watched Tzolis play for his country against Sweden in June and was suitably impressed.

So far, the 24-year-old looks a positive addition to Arteta's squad.

Arsenal, who also made Piero Hincapie's loan deal permanent and signed Illan Meslier on a free transfer, are happy with the signings they have made.

The captures of Guimaraes and Konsa, who will both be 30 by the end of next season, have raised eyebrows given the combined Â£126m fee, amid concerns over how the pair's longevity may impact the natural evolution of the squad.

Yet it is undeniable that Guimares and Konsa add elite quality and experience to Arsenal ranks, and ultimately the club feel they paid the going rate to get those deals over the line.

Vinicius Jr signed a upcoming six-year deal at Real Madrid in August.

While the club delivered proven talent for Arteta in defence and midfield, Berta's remit of adding an elite attacker ended in disappointment.

Rogers was the club's primary target heading into the window, and the early indications were positive amid a strongly held view internally that the forward wanted to join.

At the start of the summer, it was Arsenal's understanding that Villa valued Rogers at Â£100m. Arsenal valued Rogers at Â£80m.

Berta, however, was confident of negotiating the price down to a level he and the club believed could get the deal done.

In the meantime, however, Berta explored alternatives - Bradley Barcola, Kenan Yildiz, Yan Diomande and Nico Paz were admired.

Anthony Gordon was a long-term target, but he had agreed before the World Cup to join Barcelona.

According to recent reports, yildiz and Paz will continue to be realistic targets moving forward. Eli Junior Kroupi is another the club will watch once he returns from injury for Bournemouth.

Anderson's move from Forest to City for Â£116m, however, altered the complexion of Villa's outlook on Rogers' future.

Villa increased their valuation to Â£120m and ultimately Chelsea ended up signing the attacker for Â£117m.

Arsenal, it is understood, were given the opportunity to match Chelsea's offer but refused, believing their Â£80m valuation was fair - but it does beg the question of whether Rogers would be a Gunners player now if Berta had acted sooner.

Ultimately, the failure to land Rogers arrived as the first of a series of blows to Berta in his efforts to deliver a top-class left-sided attacker for the team.

Arsenal genuinely believed they had a realistic chance of signing Vinicius Jr before he decided to sign a new contract at Real Madrid.

Sources indicate that berta and Arteta were all in on the Brazil icon. The club were prepared finance the deal too.

While the transfer would likely have cost a British record fee and been one of the most lucrative remuneration packages in Premier League history, the benefit to Arteta's team and the Brazil superstar's commercial value meant Arsenal were absolutely prepared to complete the deal.

Yet well-placed sources expressed to BBC Sport over the summer that Vinicius did not want to leave Real, while others feared Arsenal were being used to strengthen the attacker's efforts to secure a more lucrative contract at the Bernabeu.

Those concerns came to fruition as Vinicius signed a latest long-term contract in Spain in another Arsenal disappointment.

There were similar reservations about Arsenal's well-documented pursuit of Julian Alvarez.

The Atletico Madrid forward demonstrated very little indication that he was willing to join Arsenal; his preference to join Barcelona was one of the worst-kept secrets of the window.

But Atletico's point-blank refusal to sell to Barcelona was deemed reason enough by Berta and Arteta to persist with their interest in the hope of Alvarez changing his mind until the closing days of the window.

Alvarez, however, preferred to stay at Atletico, even though his relationship with the club is at an all-time low.

It has been revealed that did Arsenal waste their time with Vinicius and Alvarez? The answer varies depending on who you speak to.

When it became clear Alvarez was unlikely, Berta explored his options.

Intriguingly, Arsenal have admired Chelsea striker Joao Pedro, who was deemed not for sale over the summer, although there were concerns over how he would fit into Arteta's system.

It is claimed Berta relies significantly on his vast network of agent connections rather than acting on the club's existing scouting information when analysing the market.

For example, last summer, when all the scouting information pointed towards a move for Benjamin Sesko, Berta's arrival meant the club pivoted to Viktor Gyokeres, who is presently second-choice striker.

This summer the club's late dalliance with Lyon winger Malick Fofana provided a further example of Berta leaning on his agency connections after management agency Roc Nation offered Arsenal an opportunity to sign the Belgium international.

Berta's relationship with Roc Nation was particularly prevalent this summer given Arsenal's pursuit of Vinicius and the sale of Gabriel Martinelli, who are both clients of the agency.

It remains to be seen how much of an impact Arsenal's failure to sign a recognised top-level attacker impacts their season, particularly in light of Martinelli and Leandro Trossard's departures.

Arsenal headed into the window with a clear remit of ensuring the club become more sustainable and adept at trading.

Part of that directive is to ensure the club remain compliant with domestic and European financial regulations.

Depending on who you talk to, the size of the potential deals for Vinicius or Alvarez would have raised doubts over Arsenal's ability to stay within the regulations.

Nevertheless, ensuring they maximised the benefits of player trading will become an increasing part of Arsenal's financial operation in the future.

It has been revealed that there was already evidence of that through the sale of Martinelli, whose Â£60m exit to Al-Hilal was the club's record departure. Arsenal have also secured a sell-on clause in the deal.

The exits of Martinelli, Trossard, Gabriel Jesus, Christian Norgaard, Jakub Kiwior, Fabio Vieira and Karl Hein secured the club in the region of Â£114m.

Through intermediaries, a possible exit for Myles Lewis-Skelly was explored, with a fee of about Â£80m believed to have been mooted for the midfielder.

Manchester United, who were attracted to Lewis-Skelly's ability to play at left-back, were interested but ultimately deemed his valuation too high.

Of course, it is Berta's job to have a firm grasp on the level of interest in the club's players and their market value but, nevertheless, the thought of Lewis-Skelly's departure resulted in huge uproar from supporters.

As BBC Sport revealed last month, the Gunners resisted any temptation to sell Ethan Nwaneri on a permanent deal, the academy graduate landing a season-long loan deal to Borussia Dortmund that includes a January recall option if required.

The minimum Â£15m fee secured in Trossard's deal to Besiktas is also viewed as a good deal inside the Emirates given the Belgian turns 32 in December.

Having spent nearly Â£450m in 12 months, Berta's work in the market has helped the club deliver their first league title in 22 years.

Yet, despite the money splashed, there remain clear problems in the squad - certainly in attack.

The summer window has left many supporters questioning Berta's body of work at Arsenal.

And with the average age of the squad increasing following the captures of Konsa and Guimaraes, can the current options build a dynasty of success before the club need to spend heavily again on regenerating the team?

Are Arsenal taking a risk in not signing a world-class forward?

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The biggest roster of the year for the U.S.
  • The tournament serves as the World Cup qualifiers, and four teams will earn spots in the 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup, with future Olympic spots also in play.
  • It has been revealed that in just nine short days, eight teams will compete in a quarterfinal round.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The biggest roster of the year for the U.S. women's national team is here. Head coach Emma Hayes has named a 23-player roster for the upcoming 2026 Concacaf W Championship.

The tournament serves as the World Cup qualifiers, and four teams will earn spots in the 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup, with future Olympic spots also in play. Fans can watch all the Concacaf W Championship matches on Paramount+.

It has been revealed that in just nine short days, eight teams will compete in a quarterfinal round. The U.S. and Canada earned direct byes into the tournament as Concacaf's top two ranked teams, and six teams now join them after a preliminary qualifying round. The USWNT will face El Salvador on Nov. 27 in the quarterfinal round, and if they advance, they'll clinch a spot in next year's World Cup. The other matchups are Canada against Panama, Mexico vs. Haiti, and Jamaica will play Costa Rica.

"It's been a great year of growth and learning for our team, and for a long time the focus has been on qualifying for the World Cup, so now that time has arrived," mentioned Hayes.

"I want to see relentless consistency from our players, individually and as a team, and I want us to be elite in both penalty boxes. If we can achieve that, I'm confident those performances will carry us through to meet our standards and goals. This is my first Concacaf event and the first for many of our players, so we're all looking forward to the experience.".

In a recent development, hayes selected a full roster that features several players competing in their first-ever senior-level World Cup qualifying tournament, and a handful of veterans. Just eight of the 23 players selected were members of the 2022 Concacaf W Championship roster: forwards Mallory Swanson, Trinity Rodman, Sophia Wilson, and Ashley Sanchez; defender Emily Fox; and midfielders Lindsey Heaps, Rose Lavelle, and Sam Coffey -- who joined mid-tournament that year.

Industry observers note that coffey returns to the roster after missing two previous international windows while managing a lower-leg injury. Defender Naomi Girma is out as she continues to manage a lingering calf injury. The centerback has not featured with the national team since April, and has yet to play with Chelsea FC this season. Midfielder Olivia Moultrie is right now rehabbing from an ACL injury sustained in August. Other notable omissions on the roster are Jaedyn Shaw and Ally Sentnor, both of whom have been part of U23 and senior camps throughout the year.

It has been revealed that this is just the third camp for the attacking line of "triple espresso" since the 2024 Olympics. If the trio starts a match during the Concacaf W Championship, it will be the first time they start a game together since the gold medal match. Both Swanson and Wilson have worked their way back into senior camps over the year following maternity leave.

Listed by position (club; caps/goals).

Goalkeepers (3): Claudia Dickey (Seattle Reign FC; 12/0), Mandy McGlynn (Utah Royals FC; 6/0), Phallon Tullis-Joyce (Manchester United, ENG; 8/0).

Defenders (8): Tierna Davidson (Gotham FC; 72/3), Kate Del Fava (Utah Royals FC; 1/0), Emily Fox (Arsenal FC, ENG; 80/1), Avery Patterson (Houston Dash; 15/1), Tara Rudd (Washington Spirit; 12/0), Evelyn Shores (Angel City FC; 0/0), Gisele Thompson (Angel City FC; 12/0), Kennedy Wesley (San Diego Wave FC; 9/1).

Midfielders (6): Croix Bethune (Kansas City Current; 7/1), Sam Coffey (Manchester City, ENG; 46/5), Lindsey Heaps (Denver Summit FC; 180/40), Claire Hutton (Bay FC; 22/1), Rose Lavelle (Gotham FC; 124/29), Lily Yohannes (OL Lyonnes, FRA; 22/1).

Forwards (6): Michelle Cooper (Kansas City Current; 16/1), Trinity Rodman (Washington Spirit; 59/13), Ashley Sanchez (North Carolina Courage; 30/4), Mallory Swanson (Chicago Stars; 105/39), Alyssa Thompson (Chelsea FC, ENG; 34/4), Sophia Wilson (Portland Thorns FC; 65/25).

In a recent development, ashley Sanchez's return to the roster comes after standout performances against Spain last window and a stellar 2026 NWSL regular season where she won the Golden Boot with 20 goals scored. She was also nominated for the 2026 NWSL MVP award. A positional shift to left winger and an outrageous amount of scoring have all led her back to the USWNT due to consistent performances, a key factor for Hayes with her large player pool.

"Be consistent first of all in performance. Ashley Sanchez wasn't on our radar, not because she isn't talented, but there were certain things we demanded from the performance that I think she has delivered in her game on a regular basis. So, I think that's the first thing. I think you've seen that includes Croix Bethune coming into this camp -- been outstanding in the number 10 position all year, and would have been in last camp as well if she was fit. You do have to consistently find consistent performances, particularly if you're a player that doesn't have credit in the bank," Hayes said.

In a recent development, as the World Cup gets nearer, finalizing a roster for the 2027 summer tournament is even closer. Things like consistent form and senior-level experience will come into play when naming a final 23 for the World Cup for Hayes.

In a recent development, "If you're a Mallory Swanson and delivered on a world stage on a regular basis for the national team, it does alter things slightly. No, we don't want players that are in our group that are in a place where they're not fighting to improve every day or be as competitive as they could possibly be, but I think when players have stacked and accumulated a lot of experience over a period of time, that is always going to put them in a steady position," Hayes explained.

Recent findings suggest that "But it doesn't guarantee anything. I will be unafraid to leave anybody off that plane if I don't feel that they are applying themselves to put ourselves in the best possible position to compete. Which is why this upcoming camp, our job is to qualify for the World Cup, and so everything we have worked towards is ensuring that every player that comes in at camp makes sure they lift their level and they position the team to have the most positive outcome, regardless of the opponent. And I'd be demanding as much as I always do, but I have a significant expectation from our senior players to step up.".

El Salvador is the eighth-ranked team in the Concacaf W Championship and earned its spot following a preliminary qualifying round. The group is coached by manager Eric Acuña, who recently made headlines for harshly criticizing his players in a press conference following losses to Paraguay last month.

Still, Hayes and the staff aren't taking any opponent lightly no matter the rankings or state of the locker room.

Recent findings suggest that "It's a team that knows is competing for something, so it doesn't matter the opponent; they're competing to go to a World Cup, and do I think that will be it will be demanding and taxing? And yes, I do. In many different ways, because the expectations are all on us. I think for them, it's how are they going to disrupt us and make it difficult? But they have two players in the front line that can cause a lot of problems, particularly in transition. So we have to set up for that," Hayes mentioned.

According to recent reports, "I think when it when it comes to the players, I've always championed creating positive environments for players. And yeah, I'm sad for the players to hear what they've gone through, but as always, I can't control that. I want the best for players all of the time in their environments, but I am here to represent the U.S. and try and help us qualify for the World Cup. So my focus is on that. Even if my heart goes out to the players and I think we still have a lot of work to do in the women's game to keep driving female-centered, female-lens environments where women can thrive.".
